speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what have been the success rates of (i) the Career Support Programme (ii) the Professional Conversion programme and (iii) the P-Max Programme so far; and (b) whether the Ministry will increase the number of intakes for each programme or improve the system including the extension of grants from one year to three years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This will benefit more than 1,000 PMETs a year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: For mature PMETs who are made redundant, we are helping them to find new employment by providing wage support for the first year of employment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is done through the Career Support Programme (CSP).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We expect this number to exceed 1,000 by the end of the year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Together with the tripartite partners, WSG will continue to raise the awareness of these Adapt and Grow programmes among workers and businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We will continue to expand our capacity to support more workers and employers as we go through this economic transition.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We will also continue to refine these programmes to ensure that they are effective in helping workers and businesses to adapt and grow.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And will the Ministry reach out to more businesses or companies to start these programmes, in order to reach out to more affected workers?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As I mentioned, this year alone, we have helped about 6,400 employees.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I do not have a breakdown in terms of the number of employers, but if we look at that number, we can easily estimate that the number of employers would be in the thousands as well.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Looking at the structural challenges that we are facing in terms of unemployment, there are three Page: 9 types of mismatches, as the Minister would be aware.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The jobs mismatch, skills mismatch and expectations mismatch: both on the part of the employee as well as the employer.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Many of our Adapt and Grow programmes, rightly, address the skills mismatch.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: So, I hope the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) can work closely with the tripartite partners to address also the expectations as well as the jobs mismatch factors.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I have noticed quite a number of such cases in the course of our dealings with many of the retrenched workers, but clearly amongst the professionals, managers and executives (PMEs), where they have a bit of a challenge.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: One is that of a mismatch, meaning that the PMETs looking for jobs and the jobs looking for PMETs, due to an information gap, are both not able to find each other.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The second type of challenge is the mismatch, meaning that they have found each other, but either the jobs do not find the jobseekers suitable, or vice versa.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Under our Adapt and Grow programmes, we are trying to address both.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, if you talk about the case of the expectation gap, in fact, this is exactly what the CSP is about.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: CSP is to bridge the expectation gap in terms of wages between employer and employee, and this is the reason why we provide this wage support for the first year of their employment so that, hopefully, after one year, both sides' expectation gap can be narrowed and they continue from there.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Having said so, certainly, there is a lot more that we need to do and can do.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I really appreciate that the Labour Movement is playing a very active part in this whole exercise.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The e2i is a very important part of our employment and Career Support Programme, and I hope that the National Trades Union Congress and the Labour Movement will continue to partner MOM, together with the tripartite partners, and do more for our PMETs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: But does the Ministry track other measures of performance, for instance, that could include the number of sectors which are being covered through these placements as well as the number of PMETs who drop out after being placed?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Yes, if we look at the numbers presented, these are the overall numbers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But in terms of actual tracking, we track by sector.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, of the PMETs that we supported so far, we keep track of what percentage of them are below 40 years old, between 40 and 50, and above 50.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As pointed out by the Member, we also track in terms of which are the most so-called popular sectors and which are the sectors where there are most openings.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, our programmes are not at the national level.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In fact, all our Adapt and Grow programmes are sector by sector.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, on the whole, we try to be as comprehensive as possible in our outreach.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As to the question about retention, for some of our schemes, we do attach a condition.
